the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports');   <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }

       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="645mm" height="43.8mm" viewBox="0 0 645 43.8" data-device="s9301-32db" data-view="left" data-switching-capacity="8 Tbps" data-packet-buffer="82 MB" data-power-typical-w="291.6" data-power-max-w="892.9" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="100 to 240 V, 12 A per feed" data-input-dc="-40 to -75 V, 40 A per feed" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 active-active hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="5+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="back-to-front" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Trident4-X9 BCM56780" data-cpu="Intel Skylake-D 8-core @ 1.9 GHz" data-memory="32 GB DDR4" data-storage="1x 128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2620" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4 with 400G ZR/ZR+ support (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'); the HIG recommends Cat 5e for the RJ45 OOB port and names no SFP+ optic, so no specific module list is published for this pair" data-zr-capacity="up to 4 OpenZR+ transceivers in a front-to-back airflow build and up to 2 in a back-to-front build, and OpenZR+ modules must not sit in adjacent ports (HIG Port Overview, Figures 12 and 13)" data-console="RJ45 RS-232, 115200 8N1, no flow control (labelled IOIOI)" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M plus 2x SFP+ 10G, both types reaching the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`

the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'); IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="645mm" height="43.8mm" viewBox="0 0 645 43.8" data-device="s9301-32db" data-view="left" data-switching-capacity="8 Tbps" data-packet-buffer="82 MB" data-power-typical-w="291.6" data-power-max-w="892.9" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="100 to 240 V, 12 A per feed" data-input-dc="-40 to -75 V, 40 A per feed" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 active-active hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="5+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Trident4-X9 BCM56780" data-cpu="Intel Skylake-D 8-core @ 1.9 GHz" data-memory="32 GB DDR4" data-storage="1x 128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2620" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4 with 400G ZR/ZR+ support (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'); the HIG recommends Cat 5e for the RJ45 OOB port and names no SFP+ optic, so no specific module list is published for this pair" data-zr-capacity="up to 4 OpenZR+ transceivers in a front-to-back airflow build and up to 2 in a back-to-front build, and OpenZR+ modules must not sit in adjacent ports (HIG Port Overview, Figures 12 and 13)" data-console="RJ45 RS-232, 115200 8N1, no flow control (labelled IOIOI)" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M plus 2x SFP+ 10G, both types reaching the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }

the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'); the HIG recommends Cat 5e for the RJ45 OOB port and names no SFP+ optic, so no specific module list is published for this pair" data-zr-capacity="up to 4 OpenZR+ transceivers in a front-to-back airflow build and up to 2 in a back-to-front build, and OpenZR+ modules must not sit in adjacent ports (HIG Port Overview, Figures 12 and 13)" data-console="RJ45 RS-232, 115200 8N1, no flow control (labelled IOIOI)" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M plus 2x SFP+ 10G, both types reaching the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='ufispace/fan-405637@'] .state-fault { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/fan-405637@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-fail { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-input-lost { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-input-lost { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-standby { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-standby { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-warning { --led-color: #22c55e; --led-color-alt: #ef4444; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-132-dc@'] .state-warning { animation: portrayal-alternate 1s linear infinite; }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="645mm" height="43.8mm" viewBox="0 0 645 43.8" data-device="s9301-32db" data-view="right" data-switching-capacity="8 Tbps" data-packet-buffer="82 MB" data-power-typical-w="291.6" data-power-max-w="892.9" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="100 to 240 V, 12 A per feed" data-input-dc="-40 to -75 V, 40 A per feed" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 active-active hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="5+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Trident4-X9 BCM56780" data-cpu="Intel Skylake-D 8-core @ 1.9 GHz" data-memory="32 GB DDR4" data-storage="1x 128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2620" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4 with 400G ZR/ZR+ support (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'); the HIG recommends Cat 5e for the RJ45 OOB port and names no SFP+ optic, so no specific module list is published for this pair" data-zr-capacity="up to 4 OpenZR+ transceivers in a front-to-back airflow build and up to 2 in a back-to-front build, and OpenZR+ modules must not sit in adjacent ports (HIG Port Overview, Figures 12 and 13)" data-console="RJ45 RS-232, 115200 8N1, no flow control (labelled IOIOI)" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M plus 2x SFP+ 10G, both types reaching the x86 (HIG Connecting the OOB Management Cables)" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }

the eight QSFP-DD ports also take 200/100G" data-optics-qsfp56="200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4 and 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~23 as 200/100G" data-optics-sfp-plus="10G on the out-of-band management pair (datasheet '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports');   <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
